### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **66** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5a04db8b66c157753a53d459a126ea8ffb9afedf` — the merge of head `71324295d471099c8ab8926e1b44ddace72ce7ae` into base `f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5a04db8b66c157753a53d459a126ea8ffb9afedf && git checkout 5a04db8b66c157753a53d459a126ea8ffb9afedf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7 71324295d471099c8ab8926e1b44ddace72ce7ae && git checkout -B drift-repro f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7 && git merge --no-ff 71324295d471099c8ab8926e1b44ddace72ce7ae

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f44758b21e61094570ee9c04bfe26f228ffefdf7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: REWORK at `9a099c3d2185545c884facf47618d8041a5d0a53` (2026-11-20T17:47Z). A changeset sentence and the ablation record

**Scope.** I reviewed the 16 files against merge base `eb9f8ed801` (+1,114 / −20). The dev report is 7046516194 and the claim is 7043112112.

The compile, the refusal, the Turso remote face, the chokepoint exemption and the case-set hold. Two things are owed. The changeset claims PostgreSQL coverage that the dev's own O2 measurement contradicts, and the report records no ablation.

### What I checked

- **The compile** (`fixedReadLeafSubquery`, `sql-driver-internal-helpers.ts`).
  - It builds `getBuilder(table).select(column)`, then the leaf's own `equals` and `memberOf` predicates, then `whereNotNull`, then `<> ''` except on Oracle (`emptyStringIsNull: this.isOracle`). Every value is bound.
  - There is no `applyTenantScope` on the inner builder, as ① ruled A. The outer builder keeps its wall.
  - The `$in` arm of `applyFilterCondition` embeds the subquery in the list's own position, `whereIn` or `orWhereIn`.
  - I agree with keeping the walled `readableIdsSubquery` and the unwalled inner read deliberately different. ✔
- **The walk** (`findMisplacedFixedReadLeaf`).
  - It treats `$and` and `$or` members, `$not`, and a composed scope (and on the remote face, a resolved semi-join's scope) as nodes, and a field's value as an operator map.
  - A field's `$in` comparand is the one admitted position. A leaf anywhere else, including a bare field value, `$eq`, `$nin` or inside a list, is found.
  - Cycles are guarded with an on-path set.
  - `applyFilters` refuses it before compiling, through `refuseFixedReadLeafOnce` on its own per-driver flag. ✔
- **The refusal is INTERNAL_ERROR / 500, not INVALID_FILTER.** I agree. ADR-0155 holds a fixed-read leaf refusal at 500 wherever it occurs, as the step-2 seam does (#35839). The dispatch text was the error, not the dev. The pins assert `{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', status: 500 }`, plus one `error` log per driver on both Turso faces. ✔
- **Turso.**
  - Local and embedded-replica modes inherit the SqlDriver compile.
  - The remote transport's `fixedInnerReadSQL` builds the same statement from the same exported predicates, with `emptyStringIsNull: false` because libSQL is SQLite.
  - `TursoDriver` walks and logs first, and the transport throws the unlogged envelope.
  - The pins check the transport's statement text and bindings. ✔
- **`check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs`.** It adds exactly one EXEMPT entry, keyed `…::fixedReadLeafSubquery::inner`, with the ruling cited, and the summary line counts it. `scripts/` is not a governed path. ✔
- **The case-set** (`@objectstack/spec`).
  - `n5` reaches `d7`, whose only grant is stamped in `org_b`.
  - The new nested-under-tenant case carries `requiresUnwalledInnerRead: true` and `tenantId`, so the existing spec test that every such case is tenant-read holds.
  - Its note names the failure it discriminates: a walled inner read drops `n5`.
  - `Clause-②: yes` and patch on spec are right for a published fixture whose expectations widen. ✔
- **CI at `9a099c3d21`:** 58 success, 11 skipped, 0 red, as relayed. ✔

### Required

1. **The changeset overclaims PostgreSQL.** It says the compile "covers every read verb and `updateMany`, on SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle", and that the engine's seam "now hands the leaf to these drivers".
   - The dev's O2 measurement says otherwise: on PostgreSQL, an object whose `id` column is not text (a federated table keyed by integer or uuid) fails the statement with `DATABASE_ERROR` 42883, where today's list answers the rows. `supports.fixedReadLeaves` is declared for every dialect, so once a producer writes the leaf (step 6), the engine hands it to PostgreSQL for such an object.
   - Nothing writes the leaf today, so nothing breaks now. The release note still has to say what is true when it ships.
   - **Fix:** add one sentence. For example: "On PostgreSQL, an object whose `id` column is not text (an integer- or uuid-keyed federated table) fails the statement (`DATABASE_ERROR`, 42883) instead of answering its rows: that case is open on #35872 (ADR-0155 D-0) and is settled before the sharing plugin writes the leaf." Optionally also say that MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle are pinned at compile shape here and run live in CI's Temporal Conformance job.
2. **Ablations: a record, no new head.**
   - The report has no `ablations` key. The pins are dense, but L1 takes positive controls as evidence that they discriminate. Run each mutation on the face(s) shown, and post the reds and the clean restore as a report amendment:
     - **(a) Drop the leaf.** Replace the `$in` arm with "no restriction" (`continue` before `whereIn`). The case that "returns `n3` too" should go red. Run on SQL.
     - **(b) Wall the inner read.** Add `applyTenantScope` (or a `tenantId` predicate) to the inner builder. The nested-under-tenant case and the `g7` direct case should go red. Run on SQL, and in Turso remote by adding the scope to `fixedInnerReadSQL`.
     - **(c) Skip the walk.** Make `findMisplacedFixedReadLeaf` answer `null`. The misplaced pins should go red. Run on both faces.
     - **(d) Drop the blank-id guard.** Remove `<> ''`. The `g10` and "empty id names no record" cases should go red.

### For the seat (not L1's to rule)

- **O2 / D-0** (the PostgreSQL non-text key) goes to the maintainer, with the dev's recommendation A. Until it is ruled, "Part of #35872" is the right closing line.
- **The D6 and O3 readings** are measurements for the maintainer. On PostgreSQL the owner index stops serving the total once the subquery arm is present (x2–6 at 10,000 accounts). A covering index on `sys_record_share` is the seat's to file.

### Before landing

- Delta L1 after item 1.
- CI green on that head.
- CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 PASS (`packages/spec/src/**`).

This follows my REWORK 7046597905 at `9a099c3d21`. Both required items are met.

### What changed, and what I checked

- **The diff from `9a099c3d21` is the changeset only** (`.changeset/35872-shared-record-ids-sql-compile.md`, +1 / −1). No code, pin or fixture moved, so the code findings in 7046597905 carry over unchanged.
- **Item 1, the PostgreSQL overclaim: met.** I read each new sentence against the code and the dev's O2 measurement.
  - "It compiles on every read verb and on `updateMany`" replaces "covers", and now claims the compile, not live behaviour. ✔
  - "SQLite and PostgreSQL were run live for this release. MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle are pinned at compile shape, and MySQL also runs live in CI's Temporal Conformance job." This matches the report's runs and the pins. ✔
  - The non-text `id` sentence names the dialect, the case (an integer- or uuid-keyed federated table), the outcome (`DATABASE_ERROR`, 42883, where today's list answers rows), where it is open (#35906, ADR-0155 D-0) and when it is settled (before the sharing plugin writes the leaf). ✔
- **Item 2, the ablations: met** (report amendment 7047340985). Every leg went red and every restore was clean:
  - **(a) Drop the leaf.** With the leaf skipped, 50 failed on SQL. With the leaf compiled as TRUE, 52 failed, and the nested case answered `n1, n2, n3, n5`, so the "returns `n3` too" witness is live. ✔
  - **(b) Wall the inner read.** 10 failed on SQL, including `g7`, the nested-under-tenant case, the aggregate, the tenant write and the statement pin. 4 failed on the Turso remote face. ✔
  - **(c) Skip the walk.** 18 failed on SQL, and 13 on Turso through dist. ✔
  - **(d) Drop the blank-id guard.** 12 failed: the N4 tests and the bindings pins. **My prediction was wrong here.** I named the `g10`-citing shared case as the witness, and it stays green under this mutation. The N4 tests are what discriminate the guard, so the guard is still covered. ✔
- **The closing line.** The body now says `Fixes #35872`. I accept it: O2 / D-0 has its own decision card (#35906), and #33787 is Blocked-by #35906, so nothing open on #35872 is left for this PR to carry.
- **CI at `71324295d4`:** 60 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed. ✔

### Before landing

- CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER L2 PASS on `71324295d4`, because the PR touches `packages/spec/src/**` (the case-set). That is the seat's to run.
- Undraft.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `71324295d471099c8ab8926e1b44ddace72ce7ae`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf-conformance.ts + packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/fixed-read-leaf-compile.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-internal-helpers.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, scripts/check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs

Read: card #35872 (body, triage 7042499013, claim 7043112112, reports 7046516194 and 7047340985), PR #35893 (body, 16 files, net diff from `eb9f8ed801`), ADR-0155 at the head, and the head's check-runs. The rest of the diff (the two driver suites, the spec self-test, the three `scripts/adr-anchors/` files, the changeset prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on this head: 78 runs, 61 success, 17 skipped, 0 failure, none pending. `Check Changeset` (3 runs), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Test Core` 1/10 to 10/10, `Type Check` (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger) and `Spec property liveness` are success. `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is skipped by its own selector, so no check-run on this head measured a live PostgreSQL or MySQL cell; the live PostgreSQL figures are the dev's local runs, and MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle rest on compile-shape pins.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`driver-sql` accepts a `SharedRecordIds` leaf as a field's `$in` comparand** and compiles it to `field IN (SELECT record_id FROM sys_record_share WHERE …)`. Right: it is the position ADR-0155 D1 names and the form `fixed-read-leaf.ts` on main describes ("`field IN (SELECT column FROM table …)`, where `field` is the one whose `$in` the leaf is"). Every compile path in the package enters through `applyFilters` (find, count, aggregate and its per-aggregation filter, distinct, the bulk and predicate writes, latest-per, window, query plan, the `ReadableIds` subquery), so the arm and the refusal hold on all of them.
2. **A leaf at any other position is refused before a statement runs**, `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500, logged once per driver. Right: D4 and D5 ("evaluates the leaf exactly, or refuses it loudly"), with the envelope `@objectstack/core`'s `refuseFixedReadLeafOnce` already carries on main.
3. **`SqlDriver.supports.fixedReadLeaves` is `['SharedRecordIds']`**, inherited by `SqliteWasmDriver` and by `TursoDriver` in every mode. Right for the compile, and it lands in the same change as the compile, as the card orders. The engine's seam now hands the leaf to these drivers. One known class does not answer its rows: PostgreSQL with a non-text outer key (see ③).
4. **The Turso remote transport accepts the leaf in `$in`** and compiles the same subquery from `fixedInnerReadPredicates`. Right: D5's second row. Remote mode declares the leaf only because this compiler exists.
5. **`@objectstack/driver-sql` gains five exports**: `findMisplacedFixedReadLeaf`, `fixedInnerReadPredicates`, `misplacedFixedReadLeafMessage`, and the types `FixedInnerReadPredicates` and `MisplacedFixedReadLeaf`. Right: the remote compiler lives in another package and D4 forbids it a private copy of the predicates.
6. **`SHARED_RECORD_IDS_CASE_SET` changes as data, with no export added or removed**: a fifth note row `n5`, one existing case's `expected` moves from `[n1, n2]` to `[n1, n2, n5]`, and one case is added under a tenant. Right: every consumer seeds from the set and asserts from the set, so none restates the rows. On main the only consumers of `.cases` are the spec self-test and, in this diff, the two driver suites; objectql reads `.seam`, which is unchanged.
7. **`check:tenant-chokepoint` admits one unscoped read builder**, `fixedReadLeafSubquery::inner`, where it admitted none. Right: D2 orders exactly this record ("an exemption citing this record if the guard reads the builder"), and the key silences that one binding only (`violationsOf` looks up `file::method::binding`).
8. **The driver also compiles a placed leaf on `deleteMany` and in a per-aggregation filter**, wider than D1's verbs. Right: the verb rule is the seam's, and the driver's answer there is the exact set, never an ordinary comparand.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `patch` on `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso` and `@objectstack/spec`. It matches what the diff publishes: no key, value or type a metadata author can write changes (the leaf has no authored spelling, and `DriverCapabilities.fixedReadLeaves` is already on main), so `Metadata-protocol: none`, and AGENTS.md gives `none` the level `patch` for a widening that is not a protocol change.
- `Clause-②: yes` is line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, and it is the right value: judgments 1, 3, 4 and 5 widen an accept-set or the public surface. No arm is owed, and the title carries no `!`.
- The changeset's own account agrees with the tree: it says the compile exists on five dialects, names which were run live, and names the PostgreSQL non-text-key class and its card.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **O2 on PostgreSQL, a non-text outer key (report 7046516194, question 1): escalated, correctly.** D-0 says a card that cannot keep the same rows stops and the case goes to the maintainer. It is decision card #35906 (open, `needs-user-decision`), and #33787 carries `Blocked-by: #35906` (comment 7046618774); I read both with one GET each to confirm the escalation exists. On this head the case fails with a database error at plan time, for every row set, so it is a loud answer and never a silent miss (D2), and no producer writes the leaf.
- **O2 on the other dialects: escalated to the card thread by this record.** #35906 asks its question about PostgreSQL only. Its own analysis lists MySQL and SQL Server conversion as unmeasured and Oracle `RAW(16)` keys as expected to differ, and O2 asks for every dialect `driver-sql` ships. The `$in` arm runs ahead of the Oracle uuid-comparand handling, so a `RAW(16)` outer key reaches the subquery as it stands. Before step 6 is cut, #35906's question or a card beside it should own those three dialects.
- **The refusal envelope (question 2): answered.** `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 is ADR-0155 D4's sentence ("⛔ It is not `INVALID_FILTER`") and what the seam and `fixed-read-leaf-refusal.ts` answer on main. The dispatch template's `INVALID_FILTER` wording loses to the ADR.
- **O3, the covering index: answered as a measurement, index untouched.** The carrier is the seat, as the report says.
- **D6, the caller with no grant: answered, and it is a cost.** PostgreSQL 16 stops serving the total from the owner index (a seq scan of the object's table, growing with the table). D6 makes the switch quote this, so the carrier is #33787. One unmeasured observation for that card: PostgreSQL cannot bitmap-OR a hashed SubPlan, but it can over an InitPlan array, so `id = ANY(ARRAY(SELECT …))` may keep the owner index. That form is outside D2's stated SQL and is the maintainer's to weigh.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The change is the push-down: it replaces a materialised id list with one in-database subquery. Neither compiler adds an id read, a cap, an ordering or an in-app join. The remote face binds the predicates' own values only.
- **Deviations in the reports**: the branch name is the platform's exception stated in the claim; the spec suite narrowed to `src/data` and the objectql seam test are covered by `Test Core` on this head.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf-conformance.ts`** holds against ADR-0155 and its first consumers.

- I recomputed the two nested cases from the rows. Unscoped: the doc scope `owner = u1 OR id IN G(u1)` answers d1, d2, d3, d7, d8, so the notes are n1, n2, n5. Under `org_a`: the composed scope's subquery is walled (`readableIdsSubquery` calls `applyTenantScope`), d8 leaves, and the notes are still n1, n2, n5. With the inner read walled as well, g7 (stamped `org_b`) leaves G, d7 leaves, and n5 drops: the case fails exactly the reading ① ruled A forbids, in the nested position step 1's L2 N4 asked for.
- The new case is the only way the shared set can tell a walled inner read apart inside a composed scope: the direct case cannot, because there the arm under test is at depth one.
- The empty-id half of N4 is not in the shared set, and that is right: a doc with an empty id would enter every evaluator's row set. Both driver suites witness it locally.
- `driver-memory` refuses a tenant-scoped call, and the module's own rule already says such a driver records the refusal for every case that carries `options`, so the new case does not strand step 4.

**The implementing files agree with the contract.**

- `fixedReadLeafSubquery` builds what D2 writes: the table and column from the leaf's description, each `equals` and `memberOf` bound, `IS NOT NULL`, the not-equal-to-empty half except on Oracle, no `applyTenantScope`, no limit, no order. `record_id` is a keyed text field with `maxLength: 100`, so it is created as `varchar(100)` on every dialect, Oracle included, and the comparison is varchar to varchar on the tables the platform manages.
- The inner columns are unqualified, and every one is a column of `sys_record_share`, so none can bind to an outer table in the nested position.
- `findMisplacedFixedReadLeaf` returns a finding only for a value `isFixedReadLeaf` vouches for, so it cannot refuse a filter that holds no leaf. The one position it passes, a field's operator map `$in`, is the position both compilers compile: `compileFilters` routes any map holding a `$` operator to `applyFilterCondition`, whose `$and`, `$or`, `$not` and operator-map branches match the walk's roles. I found no position the walk admits and a compiler reads as a value.
- On the remote face a placed leaf survives `replaceComposedReadableIds` (it copies only nodes it rewrites) and `toRemoteFieldSpec` (a non-list `$in` passes by reference), so the brand reaches the transport. Every remote door with a `where` goes through `toRemoteWhere`.
- The message names the position, the leaf's name and its table, never the recipient.
- The gate's exemption text states a reason a reader can check, and its success line now counts the entries.

Nits, none with an effect on correctness or the contract:

- N1 (nit) — `RemoteTransport.fixedInnerReadSQL` names the table with `tableSql(read.table)`, where the local face resolves it through `getBuilder`'s registry and the `ReadableIds` twin through `remoteTableFor`. A managed platform table maps to itself, so the two faces agree today. Accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit) — `EXEMPT` has no liveness check: an entry whose binding is later renamed or removed stays in the table and nothing reports it. It was empty until now, so the question is new. Follow-up for the gate's owner.
- N3 (nit) — the comment on `fixedReadLeaves` in `sql-driver.ts` says "every dialect" and does not name the class #35906 holds; the changeset does. The card that lands #35906's ruling edits that comment with the code.
- N4 (nit) — the walk runs once per `applyFilters` call, so once per nesting level, and up to three times on the remote face. It is linear in the filter and adds no statement.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review brief — PR #35893 @ `71324295d471099c8ab8926e1b44ddace72ce7ae` (card #35872)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths packages/spec/src/data/fixed-read-leaf-conformance.ts` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.
